findings.fsdQuote: The On Deck row shows up to 50 series.
findings.note: The On Deck row loads page 1 with a page size of 20, so it shows 20 series at first (more via the carousel's next-page loader), not 50.

findings.fsdQuote: Each row on the Home screen can be collapsed, and Kavita remembers the choice on the next visit.
findings.note: The carousel row has only a title and prev/next buttons; there is no collapse control and nothing stores a collapsed state.

findings.fsdQuote: The Home screen is the default screen and shows rows of series such as On Deck, Recently Updated Series, Newly Added Series and More In a randomly picked genre.
findings.note: The root path redirects to home, and the dashboard renders On Deck, Recently Updated, Newly Added and More In Genre streams; the genre is picked at random.

findings.fsdQuote: Clicking the title of one of these rows opens All Series with a matching filter and sort order.
findings.note: Each row's title click builds a filter and sort (last chapter added, read progress, created, or genre) and navigates to all-series.

findings.fsdQuote: Users without the Read Only role can choose which rows appear, and in what order, from the Customize page in their settings.
findings.note: The Customize settings tab is hidden from users with the Read Only role.

findings.fsdQuote: The library screen shows the library's name, its actions menu and the number of series it holds.
findings.note: The header shows the library name, an actions menu and the series count.

findings.fsdQuote: Series appear as cards with a jump bar for skipping to a starting letter, and several series can be selected at once for a bulk action.
findings.note: Series are shown as cards in a layout with jump bar keys and bulk operations, with selection allowed.

findings.fsdQuote: A Random button on the library screen opens a randomly chosen series from that library.
findings.note: The library screen template has no Random button and the library-detail code has no random-series logic.

findings.fsdQuote: The filter panel builds rules on fields such as genre, tag, people, read progress, rating and publication status, and the rules can match all or any of them.
findings.note: The metadata builder offers an And/Or combination selector over the filter statements.

findings.fsdQuote: Results can be sorted by a chosen field in either direction and limited to a set number, and a filter can be named and saved as a smart filter.
findings.note: The panel has a limit input, sort field select with an ascending/descending button, and a name input for saving a smart filter on series.

findings.fsdQuote: All Series lists the series from every library the user can access, with the same filter panel and bulk selection as a library screen.
findings.note: All Series uses the same card layout with a filter panel and bulk operations.

findings.fsdQuote: The arrow beside the Read button offers the same action in incognito mode, which does not save progress.
findings.note: The split dropdown beside Read has one item that reads in incognito mode (glasses icon).

findings.fsdQuote: A star button adds the series to Want to Read or removes it.
findings.note: A star button toggles Want to Read with an add/remove tooltip.

findings.fsdQuote: The Edit button is shown only to administrators, and the Download button only to administrators and users with the Download role.
findings.note: The Edit button is wrapped in an admin check, and the download button is only rendered when canDownload() is true.

findings.fsdQuote: in book and light novel libraries the Volumes tab is called Books.
findings.note: The Volumes tab title switches to Books when the book logic applies.

findings.fsdQuote: Manga series open on the Volumes tab by default.
findings.note: For manga libraries the default tab is Storyline; Volumes is only the default for book/light novel libraries.

findings.fsdQuote: The Reviews tab appears on a volume only when the volume holds a single chapter.
findings.note: The volume's Reviews tab is wrapped in a check that the volume has exactly one chapter.

findings.fsdQuote: has a Related tab listing the reading lists that contain the chapter when there are any.
findings.note: The chapter's Related tab is shown only when the chapter's readingLists list is non-empty.

findings.fsdQuote: Brightness can be set anywhere from 0% to 100%.
findings.note: The darkness (brightness) setting is validated with a minimum of 10 and maximum of 100, so 0% is not allowed.

findings.fsdQuote: A slideshow mode turns the page automatically after a set number of seconds.
findings.note: No slideshow or auto-play feature exists in the manga reader code.

findings.fsdQuote: Kavita removes a series from Want to Read automatically as soon as the user finishes reading it.
findings.note: Removal is done by a daily scheduled cleanup job that drops fully-read series from Want to Read, not immediately on finishing.

findings.fsdQuote: The Want to Read screen lists the series the user has starred, with a count and the same filter panel and bulk selection as a library screen.
findings.note: The screen shows a series count, filter panel, and bulk operations over series cards.

findings.fsdQuote: It has a jump bar but no filter panel.
findings.note: The collections screen passes jump bar keys and disables filtering.

findings.fsdQuote: The Collections screen shows every collection the user can see, with the name of the user who created it and a mark on promoted collections.
findings.note: Each collection card shows an owner component as subtitle and a promoted icon beside the title.

findings.fsdQuote: A collection's screen shows its title, number of series and actions menu, and a collection synced from an outside service also shows how many of the source's series are on this server and when it last synced.
findings.note: The header shows title, actions menu and series count; for externally sourced collections a sync progress (collected / total) and last-sync tooltip appear.

findings.fsdQuote: Its series can be filtered and selected in bulk.
findings.note: The collection detail uses the filter panel and bulk operations over series cards.

findings.fsdQuote: The series in a collection can be exported to a CSV file.
findings.note: No CSV export exists in the collection detail component or elsewhere in the repo.

findings.fsdQuote: Administrators and users with the Promote role can promote or unpromote a list from its actions menu.
findings.note: Promote/Unpromote actions on reading lists render only for admins or users with the Promote role.

findings.fsdQuote: with a Read button whose menu also offers incognito reading.
findings.note: The Read/Continue button has a dropdown with incognito (glasses) read and continue items.

findings.fsdQuote: The list's owner sees an Edit button and, on larger screens, a Reorder button.
findings.note: Edit and Reorder (hidden below md) buttons are shown only when the list is owned by the user.

findings.fsdQuote: In reorder mode each item gets a remove button, and an Order Numbers switch adds a box to each item for typing its new position.
findings.note: In edit mode the list shows remove buttons and an Order Numbers switch that enables accessibility mode.

findings.fsdQuote: A filter box for finding items appears once a list has more than 25 items.
findings.note: The filter box appears when the list has more than 10 items, not 25.

findings.fsdQuote: and only administrators see its Promote switch.
findings.note: The edit modal's Promote switch is wrapped in an admin-role check.

findings.fsdQuote: The edit dialog holds the title, which is required and must be unique, the summary, the starting and ending month and year, tags and the cover image
findings.note: The edit modal has title (with duplicate-name validation), summary, start/end month and year, Tags and Cover Image tabs.

findings.fsdQuote: The owner can share a reading list through a public link that opens without signing in.
findings.note: No public share link feature exists in the reading list UI; all reading list routes sit behind the auth guard.
A Genres browse screen lists genres; the FSD describes only People and Tags under Browse.
An All Annotations browse screen with a filter exists but is not in the FSD.

findings.fsdQuote: A new password must be at least 8 characters long.
findings.note: The server's identity options require a minimum password length of 6.

findings.fsdQuote: When Prompt on Download is on, Kavita asks for confirmation before any download larger than 500 MB.
findings.note: The size warning threshold is 100 MB (104,857,600 bytes), not 500 MB.

findings.fsdQuote: Days of Backups and Days of Logs each accept a value from 1 to 30 and both default to 30.
findings.note: Both fields are validated min 1 / max 30 and seeded with 30.

findings.fsdQuote: Cache Size must be at least 50 MB
findings.note: Cache size is validated with a minimum of 50.

findings.fsdQuote: the base URL must start and end with a slash.
findings.note: The base URL is validated with a pattern that requires a leading and trailing slash.

findings.fsdQuote: A Reset to Default button restores these settings after a confirmation.
findings.note: Reset to Default asks for confirmation, then calls the reset API and reloads the form.

findings.fsdQuote: A notice warns that changing the port, base URL, cache size or IP addresses needs a restart of Kavita.
findings.note: The page shows a notice that a restart is required.

findings.fsdQuote: Changes on this page are stored only when the administrator presses Save.
findings.note: There is no Save button; valid form changes are auto-saved after a 300 ms debounce.

findings.fsdQuote: A maintenance mode switch blocks all non-admin users from signing in until it is turned off.
findings.note: No maintenance mode setting or switch exists on the General page or in the server settings.

findings.fsdQuote: The Login role is selected by default, and choosing Admin locks the other roles.
findings.note: The invite form defaults roles to Login, and other roles are disabled when Admin is selected.

findings.fsdQuote: If the invite email cannot be sent, the form shows the invite link so the administrator can pass it on.
findings.note: The invite response's emailLink is stored in a signal that is shown and disables further sending.

findings.fsdQuote: An invite can be given an expiry date, after which its link stops working.
findings.note: The invite form has no expiry field.
